description: PROP-M3-lowest-priority is listed Tier-1 required in verification-architecture.md (line 48): 'REQ-M3 (pick_next with a normal ROI item + a cadence-elapsed reconciler item → normal item wins if its ROI > 0)'. REQ-M3 further mandates: 'A dedicated PROP-M3 test parametrizes a normal earner item (roi=100, prob=0.01 → score 1.0) vs the reconciler (score 0.0) and asserts the earner wins.' Neither test_reconciler.py nor test_reconciler_integration.py contains such a test. The integration test only exercises a menu with the reconciler as the sole item (line 46-57 in test_reconciler_integration.py), which does NOT test the priority-ordering guarantee — it only tests that when the reconciler IS picked, the in-process branch runs. Without a real earner-vs-reconciler priority test, we have no evidence the reconciler will actually stay in the intended lowest-priority slot; a scoring regression in lib/menu.pick_next could silently promote the reconciler over live earners.

evidence.snippet: | PROP-M3-lowest-priority | 1 | true | REQ-M3 (pick_next with a normal ROI item + a cadence-elapsed reconciler item → normal item wins if its ROI > 0) |
